title: Leasing SunPath Systems on More Than One Home
content:
**Desk guidance — SunPath Solar Lease, customers with several homes.**

A customer may lease SunPath systems on any number of homes they own, and each home carries one lease. There is no maximum number of SunPath Solar Lease holdings per customer.

### The rule in two parts

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| How many homes may one customer lease SunPath systems on? | Any number of homes the customer owns; no per-customer limit applies. |
| How many leases does one home carry? | One. |

### Hypothetical illustrations

- A customer who already leases a SunPath system on one home they own, and who owns a second home, is not limited by the number of leases they already hold: the count of their existing SunPath leases is not a ground for refusing a lease on the second home.
- A customer who owns three homes, each carrying its own SunPath Solar Lease, holds three leases — one per home — and no more than one on any of them.

### Points of judgement

- The count that matters under this rule is per home, not per customer: the customer's total number of leases is unlimited, while each home carries one lease.
- Each lease belongs to its own home, so the lease on one home and the lease on another are separate holdings of the same customer.
